title: Chapter 175: The Last Trump Card
html:
Chen Ge continued to dodge, but the monster eventually cornered him.

“Wait! I agree to play the game with you!”

Faced with certain death, Chen Ge “surrendered.” He slipped his phone into his pocket and looked up at the monster. “We’ll do it your way.”

Chen Ge’s abrupt change of heart made the twisted-faced man suspicious, but it only excited the monster.

“Before we begin, drop the cleaver.” This was the first time Chen Ge had heard the man speak. His voice was unnaturally sharp and shrill, as though his vocal cords had been surgically altered.

“If I win, you have to guarantee that I can leave safely.” Distrust filled Chen Ge’s eyes. The sight reassured the twisted-faced man. “Step away from the door and drop the knife. If you win, I’ll show you the way out.”

The game was designed to be unwinnable. If Chen Ge truly accepted, he faced a lifetime of torment in this dark mental hospital.

“Fine, I agree. What do I do next?” Chen Ge tossed the cleaver aside, carefully leaving its handle pointed toward him, then thrust both hands into his pockets.

“Stand right there.” The twisted-faced man advanced until only two meters separated them. “From this moment on, no matter what you see or hear, you may not make a sound. If you do, you lose.”

He stared at Chen Ge as the monster on his back stretched farther, its utterly ordinary face hanging upside down before him.

“Still silent? Then let’s make things more exciting.” The twisted-faced man crouched and bent forward. The monster pulled itself completely free of his back. It stood three meters tall. Its legs were less than a meter long, and its limbs were no thicker than an ordinary person’s, but its torso was grotesquely elongated, as though fashioned from several bodies joined end to end.

What in the world is this thing?The creature was so tall that it struggled to keep its balance, swaying as it shuffled toward Chen Ge. Only two meters separated them. Its upper body loomed over him while its lower half crept slowly closer.

As if afraid Chen Ge might change his mind, the monster clamped its spindly hands around his shoulders to keep him from fleeing. Tension coiled inside Chen Ge as it approached. He rehearsed his plan again and again, never taking his eyes off its legs.

The instant its legs drew level with the cleaver, Chen Ge tore one hand from his pocket. He held something guaranteed to injure the monster.

The pen’s sharp tip plunged into the creature’s eye. The impact immediately shattered the pen’s taped-together casing.

With the pen lodged in its eye socket, the monster writhed like a snake. The attack had clearly hurt it. At Hai Ming Apartments, Chen Ge had once thrown Xiaoxiao at the mirror monster by accident, and the doll had bitten a chunk from its body. That incident had taught him that the most effective weapon against a ghost was another ghost.

The Pen Spirit’s ballpoint pen had been part of his plan from the beginning. As the monster shrieked in pain, Chen Ge wrenched the pen free and lunged forward. He moved so quickly that by the time the twisted-faced man understood what was happening, the cleaver was already back in Chen Ge’s hand.

He had planned for this when he discarded the weapon. In the corridor’s darkness, the twisted-faced man would never have noticed that Chen Ge had left the handle pointed toward himself.

With the cleaver’s familiar weight in his hand, Chen Ge struck at the monster’s weakness—its legs. He had suffered enough that night, and the blow carried every ounce of frustration pent up inside him. With each slash, the creature’s body shrank.

The cleaver is still too weak to destroy it completely. Once it recovers, I’ll be at a disadvantage again.Chen Ge’s battle fury quickly subsided. The cleaver may not be able to kill the monster, but it can certainly incapacitate the person it depends on.

Cleaver in hand, Chen Ge snapped his head around and glared at the twisted-faced man.

“What do you think you’re doing?” Cold sweat broke out across the man’s brow. For some reason, he felt as though history was about to repeat itself.

You’re dead meat!Chen Ge charged with the cleaver raised. The twisted-faced man spun around and bolted for the stairs, Chen Ge close behind with the blade glinting ominously in the darkness. The blinded monster slithered after them like a snake, struggling to catch its prey. The three maintained a bizarre balance as the chase swept from the first floor to the fourth.

Once they entered the fourth-floor corridor, Chen Ge slowed. He realized the twisted-faced man might have been leading him here deliberately. The man had shown no hesitation at any landing; he had raced straight for the fourth floor.

Is he trying to escape into one of the other sick halls? No. He can only control the monster inside the third sick hall.Chen Ge understood how important this building was to its patients. For one reason or another, none of them would leave willingly.

Only when he was about to leave the third sick hall did the twisted-faced man finally stop. He screamed, his features contorting even further. In response, two injured men crawled from rooms on either side of the hall: Xu Tong and the patient with Phantom Limb Syndrome.

Three patients alone would not have frightened Chen Ge so badly. But from the backs of the two newcomers, more monsters were slowly emerging.

Are all the patients in the Third Sick Hall possessed by monsters? Their relationships seem more stable than the one between Zhang Peng and the mirror monster. That’s not good for me.

The Third Sick Hall had housed nine patients. Excluding Wang Shenglong, Chen Ge might have to confront eight similar creatures tonight—and some could be far more terrifying than these.

The lanky creatures slipped from the patients’ backs, and the three monsters encircled Chen Ge.

“Don’t be afraid. You’ll soon be one of us.” The twisted-faced man ordered the other two patients to block Chen Ge while he moved to lock the steel door connecting the second and third sick halls.

For a moment, the situation seemed hopeless. The three monsters had sealed every escape route and were closing in. Chen Ge doubted they would even allow him the chance to take his own life.

A three-star scenario is still beyond me.Leaning against the wall, Chen Ge drew a candy marked with a crying face from his pocket. This is my last trump card. Once I use it, I have to get out of here—no matter what.

He popped the candy into his mouth. Boundless resentment and a bone-deep chill flooded his body at once.

Long black hair crashed against the walls like waves. A profoundly malevolent presence stirred awake. Dressed in red, Zhang Ya stepped out of Chen Ge’s shadow.
